subject: generative-provider-auditing
a: Provenance.model is a required bare string, filled at all five construction sites from a caller-side constant - three of them via `process.env.X?.trim() || "baked-in-default"` (google IMAGE_MODEL, google VISION_MODEL, ollama MODEL) - and persisted with the asset as though the vendor had confirmed it
b: Provenance carries a required `modelBasis: ModelBasis` (vendor-reported | requested | undisclosed) mirroring the existing CostBasis, so a stored record states WHOSE claim its model identity is; all five sites declare `requested`, which is the honest value today
read_from: the project's own gate, tsc --noEmit, run on both arms. Measurable: provenance construction sites at which a reader can determine the basis of the recorded model identity. Arm A = 0 of 5 (gate green, nothing visible); arm B = 5 of 5 (gate green). Making the field REQUIRED is what turned tsc into the instrument - the intermediate typecheck failed at exactly five sites and enumerated them (google.ts:256, google.ts:335, leonardo.ts:190, ollama.ts:84, qwen.ts:113) rather than a reader grepping for them. lint:ratchet unchanged at baseline, 371 files, 0 errors
instrument: tsc --noEmit (project gate), both arms; lint:ratchet as the no-regression check
return_condition: per-adapter response parsing - the work that would make a genuine `vendor-reported` reachable and turn 5/5-declared into a real sourcing improvement rather than an honest label. Separately: a backfill question for already-stored records, which carry no modelBasis and are indistinguishable from confirmed ones
note: STRUCTURAL FACT, undesigned, and better evidence than the change: types.ts already carried a CostBasis discriminator with eight lines of comment arguing from a real Playground incident that 'an estimate presented as a receipt is the error worth spending two lines to make impossible' - which IS this technique's first decision rule (a request parameter is a claim by the caller; only the echoed identity is a claim by the party that did the work), derived independently, from scratch, for a NUMBER. One line above it, model sat required and unmarked. Of the four properties the subject enumerates as constituting an audited provider, this tree had modelled the epistemic status of three - cost (costBasis), custody (cleanup's named-miss enum), routing (reroutedFrom's documented meaningful absence) - and Identity, the property the golden path OPENS with, had none. The team won this exact argument three times and never noticed it applied a fourth. Every one of the five typecheck errors displayed a costBasis on the same object literal, so the toolchain printed the asymmetry five times without being asked. WHAT THIS CANNOT DO: it marks the claim without upgrading it; `undisclosed` is declared but unreached (no vendor in the roster is in that state); tsc sees construction, not persistence; and nothing REFUSES on the field, so the technique's ask - keep unattributable output out of shipping classes - is still a human who may not look.
